faqs.question: What do I do after I've been booed?
faqs.answer: Enjoy the treats, then put the paper ghost in a front window or on your door until 31 October so other players pass your house by. If you want to keep the game going, pack two bags and leave them at two homes with no ghost, usually within 24 hours.

faqs.question: How many houses do you boo after being booed?
faqs.answer: Two is the standard number, and it goes back at least to a 2005 set of instructions archived by the Wayback Machine. Some people boo more and some boo none; the 2009 beenbooed.com rules said taking part was optional.

faqs.question: Is it rude to break the boo chain?
faqs.answer: No. The game is meant to be fun, and the oldest dedicated booing site answered 'Must I participate?' with 'Nope.' Keep the ghost up so the next player skips your house, and that is enough.

faqs.question: Where can I get a you've been booed printable?
faqs.answer: We do not host a download. Copy the original rhyme and instruction lines on this page by hand or type them into any document, and draw the ghost by folding paper in half and cutting half a ghost shape against the fold.

faqs.question: When should you start booing your neighbors?
faqs.answer: Most streets start in the first or second week of October, which leaves room for the chain to travel before Halloween on Saturday 31 October 2026 or Sunday 31 October 2027. Starting the week before still works, but fewer homes will be reached.

faqs.question: What's the best time to leave a boo?
faqs.answer: Early evening, roughly between dusk and 8 pm, when it is dark enough to stay unseen but before young children and night-shift workers are asleep. Skip the doorbell where a sign asks for quiet and let them find the bag.

faqs.question: Can you boo someone in an apartment building?
faqs.answer: Yes, but ask the building manager or HOA board first, since many restrict what hangs on doors or sits in hallways. Never follow a resident through a secure entrance to make a delivery.

faqs.question: What if a neighbor's doorbell camera records me booing?
faqs.answer: Assume it will, and dress so you do not look like an intruder. If you are the one with the camera, the UK ICO says data protection law applies once footage covers beyond your own property, so think before posting neighbors' faces online.

faqs.question: What should go in a boo bag if I don't know about allergies?
faqs.answer: Use factory-sealed treats with the ingredient label left on, or go food-free with stickers, pencils or glow sticks. Avoid homemade bakes for households you do not know, since the recipient cannot ask what is inside.

faqs.question: Who started the you've been booed tradition?
faqs.answer: Nobody knows. The popular story places it in the 1990s Midwest, but we found no dated record from that decade; the earliest dated instructions we could verify are from an About.com page captured on 21 September 2005.

faqs.question: Can I boo a friend who has moved away?
faqs.answer: A doorstep boo needs someone nearby, so for someone several hours' drive away a link works better. A one-person Halloween page takes about 5 to 10 minutes to make, but it carries your name, so it cannot be anonymous.

article.contentMarkdown:
# You've Been Booed: The Neighbor Game, Its Rules and a Rhyme

"You've been booed" means a neighbor has secretly left treats, a short rhyme and a paper ghost at your door. You enjoy the treats, hang the ghost where passers-by can see it, and boo two homes that have no ghost yet, usually within 24 hours. The oldest dated set of rules we could find, archived in September 2005, allowed two days.

If the one neighbor you want to surprise has moved away, a link does the job: 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, and 38.5% of creators password-protect theirs before sending. Below: what the archives show about the origin, six steps, an original rhyme to copy out (there is no download), why the chain stalls, and etiquette for allergies, doorbells, cameras and buildings.

## What does "you've been booed" mean?

Being booed is the receiving end of a Halloween doorstep chain game, played through October before 31 October. One household leaves an anonymous bag of treats with instructions, and the recipients become the next ghosts.

The sign is the clever part: a taped-up ghost tells other players "already done," so treats spread outward instead of piling on one porch. In 2026 Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October, and in 2027 on Sunday 31 October, so the game's last delivery night is the Friday or Saturday before.

## Where did booing come from? What the archives show

The common story is that booing started as a 1990s Midwest neighborhood custom. We could not verify it: we found no dated newspaper, book or archive record from the 1990s, so treat the decade and the region as unconfirmed lore.

What we could verify is a web trail. An About.com Family Crafts page titled "You've Been BOOED", [captured by the Wayback Machine on 21 September 2005](https://web.archive.org/web/20050921011701/http://familycrafts.about.com/cs/halloween/l/blhalbooed.htm), describes the game as "sort of like a May Day basket." Its instructions ask the recipient to post a BOO sign, then within 2 days make 2 copies of the note, 2 treats and 2 signs for neighbors or friends without one.

Four years later the window had shrunk. A [22 August 2009 capture of beenbooed.com](https://web.archive.org/web/20090822130153/http://www.beenbooed.com/) gives recipients "only one day to act" and tells them to deliver after dark. Its FAQ also answers "Must I participate?" with a plain no.

## How to boo your neighbors in 6 steps

Each step gives the task, the time and the detail people skip. Times are estimates for two kits.

### 1. Read the street before you start

Note which doors already show a ghost and which have pumpkins out. Allow 10 minutes. An undecorated house may not celebrate Halloween, so a decorated door is the safer target.

### 2. Pack two kits, not one

Each kit is a bag with shop-sealed treats, the rhyme and a blank ghost. Allow 15 to 20 minutes. Keep ingredient labels on, because the recipient cannot ask you what is inside.

### 3. Write the note by hand

Copy the rhyme from the next section onto a card, with the instruction lines underneath. Allow 10 minutes. Handwriting shows a real neighbor, not a flyer drop, left the bag.

### 4. Draw the ghost sign

Fold a sheet of paper down the middle, sketch one side of a ghost along the crease, cut it out and open it. Allow 5 minutes. Write "We've been booed" across the body so the sign explains itself.

### 5. Deliver before 8 pm and step away

Set the bag where the opening door will not knock it over, ring once, and walk off. Allow 10 minutes. Walk rather than sprint on dark steps; nobody wins this game with a twisted ankle.

### 6. Hang your own ghost and pass it on within 24 hours

Once booed, put the ghost in a front window until 31 October, then restart at step 1 within a day. Skipping a turn is allowed; the 2009 rules said so outright.

## A "you've been booed" rhyme to copy out (no download)

There is no printable file here, because this blog cannot host downloads. The lines below are original to this page: copy them by hand, or type them up and print them yourself.

> A shadow tiptoed up your path,
> it left these treats and swallowed a laugh.
> Don't hunt for who, don't ask around,
> a ghost like this won't make a sound.
> Now tape the paper spook in sight,
> so no one boos this house twice tonight.
> Then pack two bags before tomorrow's dark,
> find two front doors that lack the mark,
> leave them softly, slip away,
> and pass the boo on if you'd like to play.

Add these instruction lines under the rhyme:

- Enjoy the treats. Every wrapper came sealed; read its label first.
- Put the ghost on your door or in a window until 31 October.
- Within 24 hours, pack two bags: treats, this rhyme and a blank ghost.
- Choose two homes that show no ghost yet.
- Drop them off before 8 pm and walk away quietly.
- Not up for it this year? That is fine, and the game will carry on.

For the ghost itself, two short lines fit across the paper:

- WE'VE BEEN BOOED. This house is spoken for.
- Ghosts, please float on to the next door.

## Why a two-house chain stalls, and why it still works

On paper the game explodes: if every booed home boos two more each day, one starting bag reaches 254 households in 7 days. It rarely happens, and chain-letter research suggests why.

In [Liben-Nowell and Kleinberg's 2008 PNAS study](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC2290760), which reconstructed how two massively circulated internet chain letters spread, the messages did not fan out widely in a few steps. They moved in a narrow, deep, tree-like pattern for several hundred steps. The authors' model ties this to network clustering and uneven response times.

Expect the same on a street: a thin line of ghosts winding through the neighborhood, not every door at once. A quiet block is not a failed game.

Recipients value the bag more than givers expect. In a [PsyArXiv preprint by Kumar and Epley (2021)](https://europepmc.org/article/PPR/PPR420666), givers who handed strangers small gifts, hot chocolate outdoors among them, kept guessing too low about how good recipients felt. Givers also underestimated how far their act would spread through recipients' kindness to others, which is the engine of booing.

One caution comes from a [2021 randomized trial in the International Journal of Wellbeing](https://internationaljournalofwellbeing.org/index.php/ijow/article/view/1489). Among 222 university students doing four weeks of kind acts, the biggest gains in mental wellbeing came from kindness to strong social ties. Kindness to weak ties helped less for participants with medium or high self-esteem, so booing strangers is good for the street, while a boo for a close friend may do more for you.

## Booing etiquette: allergies, doorbells, cameras and building rules

Anonymity is why the manners matter. Here are 5 rules we would add to any copy of the note.

- **Allergens:** give only factory-sealed treats with the label intact, and consider a food-free bag of stickers or pencils for a home where you have seen a small child.
- **Doorbells:** finish by about 8 pm, and skip the bell where a sign mentions a sleeping baby or a night-shift worker. Leave the bag and let them find it.
- **Cameras:** assume you will be filmed. The UK Information Commissioner's Office says that once a [home camera or smart doorbell captures beyond the owner's property](https://ico.org.uk/for-the-public/domestic-cctv-systems/), data protection law applies, so think twice before posting neighbors' faces from your doorbell clip.
- **Privacy:** never post a list of booed households, with names or addresses, in a public group.
- **Buildings and HOAs:** do not slip through a secure entrance behind a resident. Ask the building manager or HOA board first, since many restrict what can hang on doors or sit in hallways.

## Four ways to boo, compared

This table sets four formats side by side on time, cost, anonymity and the usual failure. Costs are estimates, in US dollars.

| Format | Hands-on time (est.) | Cost per home (est.) | Anonymous? | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic paper boo: treats, rhyme, ghost | 20–30 min for two kits | $5–10 | Yes | Allergens; dark steps |
| Food-free boo: stickers, pencils, glow sticks | 15–20 min | $3–8 | Yes | Small parts for under-3s |
| Building boo: apartment or HOA | 30 min plus a message to the manager | $5–10 | Partly | Hallway and door rules |
| Digital boo: a Halloween page by link | 5 min regular, 10 min premium | No materials | No, it carries your name | 48.3% of pages open on a phone |

For the street game, the paper boo wins. The digital row suits one specific person.

## A digital boo for the one neighbor you know

Some neighbors become friends, then move away. For that one person, our [interactive Halloween card for one person](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) needs roughly 5 minutes: as many as six photos, a jack-o'-lantern carved with your word, and the question "Will you be my boo?", with a bestie or family mode. It ends with a Boo License that has a "Boo someone back" option, the closest a link gets to passing the ghost on.

For more, the [premium Halloween page with a voice note and unlock time](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) needs roughly 10 minutes; on top it carries a 60-second voice note, as many as 12 photos and a reply box. You could set the unlock time to the evening your street game starts. SubhSandesh pages average 11.1 views each, reopenings included.

Both are one-person greeting pages, not a group tool. If they skip Halloween, try the [full SubhSandesh template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) instead.

### When a digital boo is the wrong choice

Skip the link for a neighbor you barely know: an unexpected message reads like spam, and our page shows your name, so it cannot stay anonymous. For an older neighbor who seldom touches a smartphone, or for children, a paper bag at the door is the better boo.

## Sources

- About.com Family Crafts, "You've Been BOOED" (Wayback Machine capture, 21 September 2005)
- beenbooed.com home page (Wayback Machine capture, 22 August 2009)
- Liben-Nowell, D. and Kleinberg, J., "Tracing information flow on a global scale using Internet chain-letter data," PNAS (2008)
- Kumar, A. and Epley, N., "A Little Good Goes an Unexpectedly Long Way," PsyArXiv preprint (15 November 2021)
- Wieners, L. et al., "To whom should I be kind?" International Journal of Wellbeing (30 September 2021)
- Information Commissioner's Office, "Home CCTV systems" (no publication date shown; under review as of October 2026)

Abstract read.

UK ICO 'Home CCTV systems' (covers fixed cameras and smart doorbells): owners should position cameras to capture only their own property; if CCTV captures someone else's property, a public area or communal space, data protection law applies. structuralLimitations: Task prompt framing '~1990s Midwest origin is common lore' could not be confirmed: no dated 1990s record found (Europe PMC full-text, Internet Archive full-text search, Google Books Ngram, Wayback CDX on likely domains; Google Books API was over quota). SERP: WebSearch (US index) returned only sports/celebrity 'booed' results with no Halloween page; the SERP was measured with DuckDuckGo HTML (lower confidence). All 10 results are small craft/mom blogs (10 weak). indywithkids.com returned a 204-word shell and was judged from its snippet.
